newsitem.title: USA: Medfly found near orange tree north of Orlando.
newsitem.headline: Medfly found near orange tree north of Orlando.

text.p: Florida agriculture officials said Friday they had set about 2,000 traps in a 4.5-mile (7-km) radius around a sour orange tree north of Orlando where a Mediterranean fruit fly was found this week.
If those traps yield a single fly, the state will begin aerial spraying of the pesticide malathion, said Maeve McConnell, spokeswoman for Florida's Medfly eradication program.
"We're taking it very seriously," McConnell said.
She said discovery of the single male medfly on Wednesday did not mean an immediate expansion of the all-out aerial attack, although it could lead to that.
Officials said they hoped fly arrived alone in Orange County by car or truck from the Tampa Bay area.
The mediterranean fruit fly, about three-quarters the size of a common housefly, does not harm humans.
Its larvae can damage more than 200 crops, but the biggest threat it poses to Floridas $8 billion fruit and vegetable industry comes from government quarantines.

The Orlando area has not been a major source of citrus since the 1980s, when hard freezes destroyed many groves. But a spreading Medfly infestation would be an unwelcome indication that Florida is losing its fight against the pest, officials said.
